A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DeepVideo-R1, with matching authors, core components, and experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and included appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-model fine-tuning experiments, benchmark results, ablations, training curves, and a qualitative example in Section 4.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and analyses and adds results on six video benchmarks in Table 2.

M1.justification: The two-component training method is retained, but its stated objective changes: v1 Eq. (9) uses an epsilon-scaled normalized log ratio, whereas v3 Eqs. (7)-(8) remove that scale and add a reference-policy KL term. These refine the reported loss; the PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: v3 adds Video-R1 training data and evaluates VSI-Bench, Video-MMMU, MMVU, MVBench, TempCompass, and Video-MME, expanding spatial, knowledge-intensive, and general temporal task coverage. It removes the Charades-STA training/evaluation and ActivityNet-Captions transfer experiment. SEED-Bench-R1, LongVideoBench, and NExTGQA remain.

E2.justification: New Table 2 adds comparisons with LLaMA-VID, VideoLLaMA2, LongVA, VILA-1.5, Video-UTR, LLaVA-OneVision, and Kangaroo. Removing v1 Table 3 also removes comparisons with grounding methods including FlashVTG, SG-DETR, VTimeLLM, and HawkEye. The retained RL-algorithm and NExTGQA comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: The added evaluations specify multiple-choice MMVU, subtitle-free Video-MME, aggregation across four TempCompass tasks, and evaluation of 4,000 MVBench questions. These introduce protocols for the new experiments. Frame sampling, encoder freezing, and NExTGQA split details for retained experiments are newly disclosed rather than established changes to earlier settings.

E4.justification: The component, difficulty-reference, augmentation-direction, and augmentation-scaling ablations remain, as do the training curves and qualitative example. However, v1 Table 3's explicit Charades-STA-to-ActivityNet-Captions zero-shot transfer test is removed, reducing the dedicated cross-domain robustness evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions explicitly state in checklist item 7 that experiments use a single run. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Figure 3's reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: v3 adds six-benchmark results and removes the grounding results and LongVideoBench perception/relation breakdowns. New Table 2 reports DeepVideo-R1-3B versus its base model at 63.1 versus 29.7 on TempCompass, but 51.1 versus 54.4 on Video-MME. Most retained scores are equivalent rounding; REBEL's SBR-L3 entry changes from 37.93 to 38.0.

T1.justification: The KL-constrained optimal-policy derivation remains, but Appendix A.3 revises the normalized-advantage identity by removing the residual epsilon factor and correcting log-ratio centering. These are mathematical corrections beyond notation changes. The revised loss nevertheless subtracts KL despite being described as minimized, leaving a new consistency problem.

C1.justification: The central claims about advantage regression, adaptive augmentation, and improved video reasoning remain. The introduction refines Reg-GRPO's claimed contribution from mitigating the vanishing-advantage problem in v1 to mitigating vanishing gradients in v3, distinguishing its role more clearly from augmentation.

C2.justification: New Appendix A discussion argues that group normalization handles preference magnitude and scale variability better than pairwise alternatives. Appendix F newly acknowledges possible overlap between pretraining and evaluation data, inherited biases, and computational and memory limitations. These substantive explanations and qualifications were absent from v1's included appendix.

D1.justification: v3 adds a repository link and extensive implementation information: software libraries, A100/H200 hardware, frozen visual encoders, group size 8, KL weight 0.1, reward-history size, frame sampling/resolution, reward definitions, and dataset splits. However, v1's exact hint-count and noise-scaling formulas disappear, leaving that part less reproducible.

R1.justification: Related work expands into knowledge-intensive, mathematical, and scientific reasoning, adds DAPO-based discussion of clipping, and provides substantive DPO/REBEL positioning in Appendix A. New benchmark and implementation references accompany these changes, while several grounding references disappear. This exceeds bibliographic updating.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method explanations, and several result discussions are extensively rewritten. Section 3.1 replaces the SFT background with PPO, and the supplement is reorganized after the checklist into Appendices A-F. Author affiliations, publication information, and acknowledgments also change.

P2.justification: v1's separate SEED-Bench-R1 and LongVideoBench tables become a denser combined Table 1, with question-category columns removed. The grounding table disappears and a six-benchmark table is added. Ablation tables are rearranged, and Figures 1-2 receive equation and diagram-label revisions; the curves and qualitative example remain.

improvement.justification: v3 broadens evaluation, corrects part of the advantage derivation, and supplies substantial implementation details and limitations. However, it removes explicit transfer evidence and augmentation-scaling formulas, while Eq. (8) subtracts KL in a purportedly minimized loss. The new Table 2 discussion also misidentifies the 3B comparator as 7B and overstates comparative performance. These benefits and losses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
